options.text: The person reads it and denies it, because it is outside the project.
options.why: Tempting. Asking is safe only when the person looks. After ten harmless prompts, the question is not read.

options.text: The person approves it without reading, after the run of harmless prompts.
options.why: Right. Approval fatigue: the dangerous prompt arrives among harmless ones and is approved by habit.

options.text: The harness blocks it, because it targets a folder outside the project.
options.why: Tempting. This board has no rule for that path; only the ask stands in the way.

outcome: The eleventh ask was approved without a look. The folder outside the project was gone, and the tests still passed.
question: The person has been asked ten harmless questions. The eleventh asks to delete ../data, outside the project. What happens?

options.text: Only a yes or a no.
options.why: Wrong. The decision has three values, allow, ask and deny, and each needs a reason.

options.text: One of allow, ask or deny, always with a reason.
options.why: Right. The learner and the log both need to know what was decided and why.

options.text: A number from zero to one.
options.why: Wrong. A permission decision is not a score.

question: A permission check returns a decision for a tool call. What must the result always carry?

options.why: Less risky. It is inside the workspace, and a rebuild restores it.

options.text: rm ../data, which reaches outside the workspace.
options.why: Right. The target is outside the project, so the same action is far riskier.

options.text: Both are the same risk, because both are rm.
options.why: Wrong. The command word is the same; the target differs.

options.text: Ask on every call, so nothing slips through.
options.why: Tempting. More asks is what causes the fatigue; the prompts left get no look.

options.text: Allow the harmless reads, deny what is outside, and ask only for what matters.
options.why: Right. Fewer prompts, and each one that is left gets a look.

options.text: Turn the prompts off so the run is faster.
options.why: Wrong. Then nothing stands between the model and the dangerous call.

question: A person is asked eleven times, and nine of the prompts were harmless reads. What should the policy do?

options.text: The allow rule, because it is the more specific one.
options.why: Tempting. Specificity is not the order. The order is fixed: ask is checked before allow.

options.text: The ask rule, because asks come before allows in the decision order.
options.why: Right. The decision order is deny, then ask, then allow, then the mode's default.
Wrong. The order of the groups decides, not the order of the list.

question: A call matches both an ask rule and an allow rule. Which decides?

options.text: A table of cases, each with the decision the policy must give.
options.why: Right. Each row is a check that can fail, which is what a test is.

options.text: The author's reading of the file.
options.why: Wrong. A reading is not a check; it cannot fail.
Wrong. The mode is only the default for calls no rule matches.
